answers.children: Yes — Clumber Spaniels are good with children thanks to their calm and patient demeanor. Their sturdy, low-slung build and gentle temperament let them tolerate handling from toddlers without protest while their determined fieldwork roots give them a steady focus even during noisy play. Living with one means a tolerant companion that prefers lounging beside the family over rowdy chasing games.
answers.other-pets: Yes — Clumber Spaniels generally get along with other pets. Their gentle and affectionate nature supports peaceful coexistence once introduced though the strong scenting ability bred for flushing game can spark occasional interest in following a scent trail. Owners live with a dog that shifts from quiet couch potato to purposeful hunter when interesting smells appear.
answers.exercise: Clumber Spaniels need 30 to 60 minutes of moderate exercise daily. Leisurely neighborhood walks or slow backyard romps suit their heavy sturdy build and low energy level while their original role flushing game in dense underbrush rewards purposeful sniffing and retrieving. Without this they pack on weight quickly turning the gentle lounger into a heavier companion.
answers.shedding: Yes — Clumber Spaniels shed moderately with some seasonal increase. Their medium-length coat on a heavy frame traps loose hair around the feathering and blocky head so regular brushing is required to keep it from settling on furniture and clothing. The result is a dog whose dignified lumbering leaves visible evidence of its presence indoors.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is hypoallergenic and the Clumber Spaniel is not one commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its medium coat with feathering sheds enough to spread dander and hair throughout the home especially during heavier periods. The gentle affectionate dog therefore demands consistent grooming from anyone sensitive to canine allergens.
answers.training: Clumber Spaniels are moderately easy to train. Their intelligence combines with a stubborn streak that can make sessions slow especially when the determined fieldwork independence surfaces instead of instant biddability. The calm patient demeanor helps once routines form yet the heavy spaniel still requires consistent guidance to prevent selective listening.
answers.lifespan: Clumber Spaniels live 10-12 years. Their heavy build and tendency toward weight gain affect daily mobility and comfort in later years while the sturdy low-slung frame bred for methodical hunting continues to support a calm indoor life. The affectionate dog therefore benefits from owners who manage its lounging habits carefully.
answers.size: Clumber Spaniels reach 55-85 lb and stand 17-20 in tall. The heaviest of the spaniels their substantial low-slung proportions create a dog that feels solidly planted and surprisingly strong when it decides to pull toward a scent. Living with one brings a gentle giant that fills laps and sofas with its blocky affectionate presence.
answers.barking: Clumber Spaniels do not bark a lot. They remain quiet most of the time offering only a low rumbling woof when something is truly amiss rather than sounding at every minor distraction. This suits their gentle calm demeanor and original role as a steady hunting companion that worked methodically without constant noise.
answers.apartment: Yes — Clumber Spaniels can live in an apartment. Their low energy calm indoor lounging and minimal barking let them settle happily in smaller spaces provided daily moderate walks prevent weight gain from their heavy frame. The affectionate dog transitions easily from field work heritage to quiet home life when exercise needs are met.
answers.first-time: Clumber Spaniels are not the easiest choice for first-time owners. The stubborn streak during training and tendency to pack on weight demand consistent management that can test novices while their determined independence from hunting roots requires patience. The gentle patient dog still rewards those who learn to guide its calm affectionate nature.
